I was able to resurrect most of the internals as the case had taken most of the impact, but the HDD was toast, those old mechanical drives don't respond well to being thrown off a balcony. Cheat engine is from the old days. "cheats" as in the random input sequences to get items or lives in games. This tool allows you to modify the memory values of the game and "cheat" a number into another. For instance changing a value that writes to another into a positive integer, say for instance enemy damage, effectively giving you god mode. Or changing the value of items held in inventory, or reputation/exp point of the pc.

Because it works on memory, if used in online games (which it shouldn't be able to anyway) it will instantly be recognized by the server as an incorrect value, possibly even raising flags on anti cheat systems. Try using this in WoW and you will get IP banned instantly.

Author: @Sneyek
Content:
Well, actually Cheat Engine allows to dynamically update memory in game. It works by letting you spy what's in memory for the program, you do one single action, rerun it, and it filter everything that changed so you can hopefully spy the variable. When you do, you can change the value.
It's fun for local single player game (Once you're done playing is normally imo) but should never be used for online game, for many reasons, first, it's bad to cheat and disrecpectful for other players, second, you'll most likely be banned for using it, and, you should also know that just having it run in the background, even just sleeping so apparently not open will probably get you banned as the game anti cheat will assume you don't have it open for nothing.

So I would recommend you to be careful and:
- Make sure to disable auto launch on startup.
- If you want to use it, make sure no game is launched, maybe even restart the computer, launch the single player game and use it as you wish.
- Once done and the game closed, close the program and restart to be safe so the PC remove any traces in memory.

Author: @lordgiacomos
Content:
13:51 Cheat engine is definitely a sus name, but is accurate as it allows messing around with specific values in various software by overwriting data at specific memory addresses (along with a bit of tooling to locate memory addresses iirc). Has legitimate usage for messing around in single player games or for figuring out how programs work.

Due to the ability for manipulating info in actively running programs, it can theoretically be used for more nefarious purposes in less secure programs, such as boosting your client's health data to give god mode on a multiplayer server (iirc, early Minecraft had exactly this exploit), or fooling a program into thinking you've paid for it (by switching a `has_paid` boolean to True on games where the DLC is already downloaded but still locked in the software) but this really doesn't work unless you already have the necessary files already, so for competent programs, this use case would require separately performed piracy, so it's not capable of much beyond maybe tricking your current WinRar session into thinking you've actually paid for it (even then, I'm pretty sure that a patch script to modify the program source code and disable the notification popups would be significantly more effective as you wouldn't have to go through the process every time you launch it).

Author: @johnthefactfddict3281
Content:
what people don't understand is that "cheat engine" is actually a MISNOMER
it is just a memory editor and scanner
ANY process can be hooked, scanned and have ram values tweaked

while yes, it is MOST COMMONLY used for video games, ANY process can be scanned and edited
I use it for Duskers, the turret having a max of 100 bullets per mission and >20 bullets per enemy(even more for swarms) is just BAD
so I tweak it and remove scrap from my inventory to reload during missions(because I am too lazy to mod the game myself)

it does only really work on single player games as the netcode causes weirdness that makes a successful "cheat" flakey if it works at all(trust me bro, I tried to mod COD to not die while trying to see the story of zombies in SP, and it was impossible without a dedicated tool)

so anyone who knows about "cheat engine" knows it is NOT a cheat, but just a memory address editor
and yes this means you can debug a program that is improperly setting variables in beta, making it more of a "memory engine" but they decided that calling it "cheat engine" wasn't stupid

Author: @dodgem259
Content:
I've worked on desktop repairs a lot longer than Linus. Having worked for HP and Dell repairing their desktops I have seen my fair share of dropped from height desktops (dropped whilst carry upstairs or fallen off a 2nd/3rd level floor in a manufacturing building) and not a single one showed the level of internal damage as this desktop has. Those graphics cards with the thick metal heatsinks on them are extremely difficult to bend to the level that that graphics has been bent, same with the CPU heatsink. The level of internal damage to the GPU and heatsink exceeds the stress levels that the glass panels would be able to take. Those glass panels would have shattered or at least cracked in multiple places.  If the desktop landed on grass there is no way the internals would be as damaged as they were because the soft ground would have lessened the impact than if it had been dropped onto concrete.

from all my extensive years of repairing desktop machines I am calling what happened to this desktop FAKE.

Author: @xBrokenMirror2010x
Content:
You've never heard of cheat engine?!?

Cheat engine allows you to modify values within any program's memory. Basically, lets say you wanted to modify your money in a game. You'd lookup values in the memory that are equal to your money, when you find the value with your money stored in it, you can modify that value to be whatever you want.

Nothing stops it from working on online games if those games don't have anti-cheat that stop memory modification. But you can still only modify values of a program running on your memory.

Oh, it also has a speedhack which lets you run programs at any multiplier of speed. Really useful, you can either slow down a program to make the game run in slow motion, or speed up the program to go fast. Really helpful stuff.

Content:
I once used the DVI on my card and used a patch cable to get the sound to the speakers.  I had a whining sound and you would think it is coil whine but _this_ was from the speakers themselves built into the monitor.  I went with an HDMI connection and no patch cable now no more whining sound.  I don't know why I didn't do it sooner.  Really the whining was not the worst thing but you definitely could have heard it.  It can be annoying at times.  It looks like the audio from the HDMI was better somehow.  Maybe it was just a much cleaner signal because if that same noise went down a cable to a TV or monitor the picture quality would probably be just atrocious assuming it even sees a signal in the first place.

So if you know someone having a whining sound tell them not to whine about it anymore and try a different connection if possible.  Of course I could transport my sisters children in my vehicle and say it makes a whining sound too LOL!!

Content: Cheat Engine is just a hex editor. you search for a number (like your level), then change it  (by leveling up), let it search for all numbers that were your last number and then changet to the new number, rinse and repeat till only one entry is left. then you change that entry to what you want, and bam, changed the ingame number. You can do that with anyhting that has a value that you can see ingame. or donwload a premade file from other ppl that has all the right codes already saved and named so you can just change it there. is really nice for replaying old rpgs, and skip the level grind. or do a run with a friend with "that weapon only", and just get the weapon start of the game or something. Author: @AnnCatsanndra
Content:
As someone who's used Cheat Engine, I can say it's pretty good for modding games, use as a trainer for speed runners that need to rehearse specific sections of a game, and a decent decompiler if trying to mod a native binary to change text / rearrange levels / inject custom DLLs, etc.

All of that said, naturally, that also makes it a tool appealing to people trying to actually *just* cheat in games, but pretty much any modern multiplayer game with even basic cheat detection will tend to just shut itself down on detection of a tool with "Cheat" in the name running or trying to access the memory. At least I seem to recall that being the case with somebody's rogue fangame-turned-malware some years back where if the text "cheat" showed up anywhere in the system, the game would immediately turn into a creepypasta and start destroying the user's system.

Author: @nico_53
Content:
Did the maths for fun, it was a simple physics problem. To calculate the final speed of the pc once it reached the ground i supposed the height of the drop to be 10 meters (i looked online the average height of 3 story buildings is about 10 meters, a bit more or less wouldn’t really affect the final speed). Using the conservation of energy we know that the potential gravitational energy the pc had before the drop is M*G*H, where M is the mass of the pc (not really important you’ll see later), G is 9.81 m/s^2, H is 10m as supposed previously. We know that the kinetic energy of a object in mouvement is 1/2*m*v^2. Using the conservation of energy, M*G*H=1/2*M*G*V^2. We can cancel the mass on both sides so G*H=1/2*G*v^2 so v=sqrt(2G*H). The final speed of the pc once it hit the groind was about 14 m/s, (the assumption i did what that the air friction was negligable). The height assumption also take in consideration the pc being trown up slightly so it reach about the roof of the building at 10 meters before falling to the ground.

The acceleration (amount of G the pc experienced when hitting the groind) depend mostly about the time of duration of the impact with the ground. The faster it happen the bigger the G are, but the final speed is more representative about the energy of impact the pc had, it being in joules.

If my assumption are correct and neglecting the air friciton the energy of impact was about 98.1 joules. (G*H).
